clue.text: Delight conveyed by French anthem

indicators.note: conveyed by says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Joy carried along by the Marseillaise.
explanation.definitionFit: To delight someone is to charm or captivate them, a synonym.

clue.text: Still in uniform

definitions.meaning: ... can mean still, as in '... more'
... also means uniform, level or consistent

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: an intensifier like 'still' and an adjective meaning level throughout.

clue.text: Some toast overwhelming defeat borne by Conservative

indicators.note: borne by means carried within, so the defeat sits inside the party abbreviation

parts.note: a rout is a crushing defeat

explanation.surface: A drink raised to a landslide loss carried by the Tories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some toast' looks like raising a glass; it is a bit of toasted bread.
explanation.definitionFit: A crouton is a small cube of fried or toasted bread, a piece of toast.

clue.text: Want to support a pronouncement of regret

indicators.note: in a down answer the lower piece supports the upper, so the word for want goes beneath the A

parts.note: lack means want or shortage

explanation.surface: A need to back a statement of sorrow.
explanation.definitionFit: Alack is an archaic exclamation expressing sorrow.

clue.text: Shape altering drastically

indicators.note: drastically suggests a radical change, so the letters are rearranged completely

explanation.surface: A form changing radically.
explanation.definitionFit: A triangle is a three-sided geometric figure, an example of a shape.

clue.text: Peasant has worthless duck (not English)

parts.note: bum is an informal adjective meaning worthless or shoddy

indicators.note: not tells us to leave the named letter out of the duck's name

parts.note: a Pekin is a breed of domestic duck

explanation.surface: A rustic owns a useless duck that isn't English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worthless' is an American usage here (a bum deal); 'not' drops the English abbreviation from the duck breed's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A bumpkin is an unsophisticated country person, close in sense to a peasant.

clue.text: Frenchman takes trains to Berkshire town

parts.note: BR stood for British Rail, the former national train operator
Eton is a town in the English county of Berkshire, home of the school

explanation.surface: A Frenchman travels by rail to Eton.
explanation.definitionFit: A Breton is a native of Brittany, a region of France.

clue.text: Potter arousing most abuse

indicators.note: arousing means stirring up, so the letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A ceramicist provoking the worst insults.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potter' looks like a maker of pots; it is the verb meaning to dawdle.
explanation.definitionFit: To potter is to idle about doing trivial things, which is to fool around aimlessly.

clue.text: Stranger beginning to keep more dark

indicators.note: beginning to points at the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: inkier means darker, more like ink

explanation.surface: A newcomer starting to keep things darker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stranger' looks like a noun for a newcomer; it is the comparative of strange.
explanation.definitionFit: Kinkier means more eccentric or odd, so stranger in the comparative.

clue.text: Wellington found here fresh enthusiasm — a new Duke?

parts.note: fresh means new
zeal is eager enthusiasm

explanation.surface: Where Wellington appears, renewed passion suggests another Duke.
explanation.walkthrough: The Duke of Wellington tempts; the definition means the city, the capital of a country.
explanation.definitionFit: Wellington is the capital city of that Pacific nation.

clue.text: Moving? Show fellow around

indicators.note: around turns the whole run of the two pieces back to front

parts.note: Evita is a well-known stage musical, a show
cove is old British slang for a man or fellow

explanation.surface: Is it touching? Give a chap the tour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' reverses both pieces as one run, so the man's word ends up first; Evita is the Lloyd Webber musical.
explanation.definitionFit: Something evocative stirs feelings and memories, so it is moving in the emotional sense.

clue.text: Wine's extraordinary strength

indicators.note: extraordinary suggests the letters of the drink's word are put out of their ordinary order

explanation.surface: A remarkable wine has unusual power.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive's S is part of the fodder here: WINES rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinew means tendon and, by extension, muscular power or strength.

clue.text: Passengers are deceived

parts.note: passengers are carried on a journey, and the same phrase for being carried also means being conned or tricked

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for being swindled is the same as the literal description of riders being transported.

clue.text: Tiny part in big hit that dominates Broadway

indicators.note: in places the small piece inside the word for the big hit

parts.note: a skyer is a cricket shot hit high into the air
a scrap is a tiny piece

explanation.surface: A small role in a smash show rules Broadway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'big hit that dominates Broadway' reads as a theatre smash; Broadway is the New York street, and a skyer is a cricket term.
explanation.definitionFit: Tall towers loom over New York streets, so the tower is what towers there.

clue.text: Plant produced by nature in generous fashion

indicators.note: produced by places the plant after the word for nature, as if nature yields it

parts.note: kind can mean nature or sort, as in 'things of that kind'
the lily is a flowering plant

explanation.surface: A flower grown by Mother Nature in an open-handed way.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something kindly is doing it generously, the adverb matching the phrase.

clue.text: Continue to discard, being desperate

parts.note: to last means to continue or endure
to ditch is to discard

explanation.surface: Keep going to throw it away, being hopeless.
explanation.definitionFit: A last-ditch effort is a final desperate attempt.

clue.text: Horse runs into aggrieved driver, originally

indicators.note: into tells us the abbreviation for runs goes inside the word for aggrieved

parts.note: sore means aggrieved or resentful
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
every driver starts out as a learner, shown by an L plate in Britain

explanation.surface: A horse bolts into an angry motorist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' tempts you to take D from driver; instead a driver at the start is a learner, L, as on British L plates.
explanation.definitionFit: A sorrel is a horse with a reddish-brown coat.

clue.text: Getting to be attractive

definitions.meaning: getting or going to bring something
... also means charming or attractive in appearance

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share one word: retrieving something and looking appealing.

clue.text: Fruit drink

definitions.meaning: a British concentrated fruit cordial diluted with water

explanation.definitionFit: Squash names both a gourd vegetable-fruit and a diluted soft drink.

clue.text: In the main, made up of States both Union and Confederate

parts.note: US is short for the United States
a confederate is an ally or accomplice

explanation.surface: A Civil War history covering both sides.
explanation.walkthrough: The Union and Confederacy of the American Civil War mislead; a confederate is any ally.
explanation.definitionFit: In the main is an idiom meaning generally or for the most part.

clue.text: Forcibly prevent others taking shower

parts.note: the rest means the others
a shower is a brief fall of rain

explanation.surface: The rest stop someone taking a wash.
explanation.definitionFit: To restrain someone is to hold them back physically.

clue.text: Suspiciously question half one's forebears

parts.note: to question is to ask

indicators.note: half takes the first four letters of the eight-letter word for forebears

parts.note: one's ancestry is one's line of forebears

explanation.surface: Doubtfully querying half of one's ancestors.
explanation.definitionFit: To look askance is to look with distrust or suspicion.

clue.text: Proposition the girl of the family in reduced circumstances

indicators.note: in reduced circumstances means cut down, so the word for the family girl is shortened

parts.note: a sister is a daughter of the family

explanation.surface: Propositioning the daughter of an impoverished family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in reduced circumstances' looks like poverty; it shortens SISTER to SIS.
explanation.definitionFit: A thesis is a proposition put forward for argument.

clue.text: Some golfers play thus all day

definitions.meaning: a putting game played around a circle of points on a green

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for non-stop activity doubles as the name of a golf practice game.

clue.text: Lights, for example, not on over central locality

indicators.note: in a down answer over places this piece above the next

parts.note: off means not on, as a switch

indicators.note: central takes the middle two letters of the word locality

explanation.surface: Lamps switched off above the town centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lights' looks like lamps; it means animal lungs sold as food.
explanation.definitionFit: Lights are the lungs of slaughtered animals, a kind of offal.

clue.text: Map — there's one inside guide

indicators.note: inside says the numeral sits within the word for map

parts.note: a plot is a plan or chart of an area, a map
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A chart with a single guide within it.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot guides ships into harbour or steers aircraft.

clue.text: Brace of fifteens playing the ultimate in rugger

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are moving about, as players do
the ultimate in takes the last letter of the word rugger

explanation.surface: A pair of rugby teams play the finest rugby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brace of fifteens' looks like two rugby sides; 'Brace' alone is the definition. FIFTEENS is rearranged and R from rugger comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: A brace is a support that stiffens something.

clue.text: Girl and boy together in boat

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl
Leon is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A young couple sit together in a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A galleon is a large sailing ship of the 15th to 18th centuries.
